finishes.note: Walls above the dado (gallery long walls, south wall, throat jambs, tribune wall), z 0.45 to the ledge 3.70: 30 mm laid finish over the travertine core, courses 1.20, blocks 1.90 +/- 30 % half-bond, 3 mm joints (the Rotunda's coursing record).
The dado z 0-0.45 on every wall, slabs 1.20 long in one course: polished and worn soft by shoulders and hands (Story: the red you cross on the dial is the red under the casts).
The lintel over the throat: soffit z 3.075 and its south face y 7.10 up to the vault's end arc.
The stair port's rough opening (jambs, head, sill) from y 31.10 to the port face, hidden behind Site's lining: the travertine core as sawn.
Structural masonry never seen: wall cores, vault shells, slab (underside z -0.40), roof (top 5.45), the sleeve round the passage, the outer faces against the ground.

The 13 niches' half-round backs and quarter-sphere heads: lime pigmented with red ochre, burnished (Pompeian). The ochre is in the plaster's body, so it is the palette's red-ochre lime, burnished (was a working, burnished.red-ochre).
The niches' floor slab at z 0.45, 0.05 thick (role guessed, as built statuary).
The 14 gallery and screen column shafts; the 4 gallery pilaster shafts (pilasters guessed).
The tribune's 12 ring column shafts; the 6 tribune pilaster shafts (pilasters guessed).
Column and pilaster bases (plinths, tori, scotia), capitals (canalis, bolsters, volutes, abacus): carved and honed.
Gallery entablature with ressauts and fillers, the screen crossing, the tribune entablature, the ring beam, dentils, the lip.
Skirting, dado rail, niche surrounds, keystones, panel frames (roles guessed: the palette names entablatures and consoles).
The 26 wall panels 0.80 x 1.90 and the lunette panel 2.60 x 0.80 (role guessed).
The 26 quadrant consoles carrying the busts (5 stand empty).
Niche plinths and pedestals, the two gallery axis plinths, the two ambulatory plinths (role guessed, with the herms).
The two herms by the stair port (plinth, tapering shaft, cap).
The centrepiece pedestal, turned, Ø 2.20 x 0.30.
The gallery barrel (R 3.8284): springing bands, plain end and pair bands, ribs and the stepped coffers (256), run in place.
The ambulatory's annular vault and its 420 coffers.
The tribune dome (sphere R 3.9464) and its 72 coffers.
The lantern end cheeks from the laylight glass (4.94) up to the vault intrados (0.04 to 0.21 high).
The gallery coffers' rosettes (256), cast, white: the palette gilds only the tribune's. Cast is the plaster's working, cast.plaster.
The rosettes in the annular vault's and the dome's coffers (492): oil-gilt, soft even lustre, dirt in the hollows.
The bead round the eye's lower edge (role guessed: gilt with the tribune rosettes).
The five laylights at z 4.94 underside (four 2.246 x 2.28, one disc Ø 2.40): laminated low-iron, acid-etched face down; Light's luminous ceiling over it.
White floor fields, borders, bands, cells and the throat: polished, worn along the walking lines.
Gallery square fields and the tribune's giallo rings and sector fields.
Frames, end panels, bands and the verde discs.

Roundels (reclaimed column slices, sectored within stock): harder than the calcite round them, they stand slightly proud as it wears. Reclaimed is the stone's provenance, not a working: it is polished (was polished.reclaimed).
The nine lozenges between the bays (role guessed: the palette's Classical Hall red).
The 41 casts after SMK's Royal Cast Collection: piece-mould seams kept, sealed with a thin size, dust on upward forms. Art makes the objects.
Closed pair of cast bronze leaves in the stair port's class opening on the port face, only while the port is unmated (on the stand).
